title: You 2.0: In the Heat of the Moment

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: So often, when we're thinking about who we are
sentences.zh: 通常，当我们思考自己是谁

sentences.en: and what we want from our lives, we think about the choices that we make.
sentences.zh: 以及我们想要什么样的生活时，我们往往会想到自己所做的选择。

sentences.en: How do we get from point A to point B?
sentences.zh: 我们如何从A点到达B点？

sentences.en: What steps can we take to improve our careers,
sentences.zh: 我们可以采取哪些步骤来改善我们的职业生涯、

sentences.en: our relationships, our personal health?
sentences.zh: 人际关系和个人健康？

sentences.en: As we ponder these questions, it can be tempting to
sentences.zh: 当我们思考这些问题时，很容易

sentences.en: assume that all we need is the right blueprint, and we can build the exact life that we want.
sentences.zh: 认为我们只需要一份正确的蓝图，就能构建出我们想要的生活。

sentences.en: But the choices we make are only part of the equation.
sentences.zh: 但我们所做的选择只是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So often, the trajectory of our lives is shaped by moments when our decision-making goes haywire,
sentences.zh: 我们的人生轨迹往往是由那些决策失控的时刻所塑造的，

sentences.en: when we act in ways that feel completely out of character.
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，我们的行为显得完全判若两人。

sentences.en: What are we to make of these moments?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何看待这些时刻？

sentences.en: What do they tell us about our inner selves?
sentences.zh: 它们向我们揭示了关于内在自我的什么信息？

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, as part of our annual You 2.0 series,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，作为我们年度“自我2.0”系列的一部分，

sentences.en: we bring you a favorite episode about certain situations
sentences.zh: 我们为您带来一期备受喜爱的节目，探讨某些特定情境

sentences.en: that cause us to become strangers to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 是如何让我们变得连自己都不认识了。

sentences.en: I definitely didn't maintain cool and calm.
sentences.zh: 我当时绝对没能保持冷静。

sentences.en: My entire body froze.
sentences.zh: 我整个人都僵住了。

sentences.en: I was just an absolute blubbering mess.
sentences.zh: 我完全成了一个只会哭泣的烂摊子。

sentences.en: I became filled with anger.
sentences.zh: 我变得怒火中烧。

sentences.en: And I just kind of lost it.
sentences.zh: 然后我整个人就崩溃了。

sentences.en: And we look at the deep psychological mystery that occurs during these moments.
sentences.zh: 我们将审视这些时刻中发生的深层心理奥秘。

sentences.en: No matter how many times we discover the strangers living inside us,
sentences.zh: 无论我们多少次发现内心住着一个陌生人，

sentences.en: the next time always catches us by surprise.
sentences.zh: 下一次发生时，我们依然会感到措手不及。

sentences.en: Quick heads up, this episode contains stories about sex, sex work, and sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 温馨提示，本期节目包含有关性、性工作和性骚扰的故事。

sentences.en: Morgan Smalley has been performing with an improv comedy troupe since she was in college.
sentences.zh: 摩根·斯莫利从大学起就一直在参加即兴喜剧表演。

sentences.en: After dozens of performances, she's learned that you need more than a creative mind
sentences.zh: 经过几十场演出，她明白要让观众发笑，

sentences.en: to get the audience laughing.
sentences.zh: 光有创造力是不够的。

sentences.en: You also need to be a good listener.
sentences.zh: 你还需要做一个好的倾听者。

sentences.en: That means not just hearing what people say.
sentences.zh: 这意味着不仅仅是听到人们说了什么。

sentences.en: You have to pick up on everything that surrounds the words.
sentences.zh: 你必须捕捉到言语之外的一切信息。

sentences.en: Like, let's say I came out, and instead of saying,
sentences.zh: 比如，假设我走出来，没有说

sentences.en: happy birthday, like, with a happy face,
sentences.zh: “生日快乐”，而是带着开心的表情，

sentences.en: I could be like, happy birthday, and clearly that means that I'm upset.
sentences.zh: 我可能会说“生日快乐”，但这显然意味着我很不高兴。

sentences.en: And then we go from there, like, why am I mad at them?
sentences.zh: 然后我们从这里展开，比如，我为什么生他们的气？

sentences.en: Is it that when it was my birthday last time,
sentences.zh: 是因为上次我过生日的时候，

sentences.en: they treated me like garbage?
sentences.zh: 他们像对待垃圾一样对待我吗？

sentences.en: Things like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Morgan prides herself on being able to pick up on subtext,
sentences.zh: 摩根以能捕捉潜台词而自豪，

sentences.en: on being able to read between the lines, behind the lines.
sentences.zh: 以能读懂字里行间、言外之意而自豪。

sentences.en: When she does that well, she can hear the results immediately.
sentences.zh: 当她做得好时，她能立刻听到反馈。

sentences.en: When you get the laugh, it's just like such a self-esteem booSt.
sentences.zh: 当你逗笑观众时，那简直是对自尊心的一种极大提振。

sentences.en: It's like instant validation.
sentences.zh: 就像瞬间得到了认可。

sentences.en: And instantly exhilarating.
sentences.zh: 而且瞬间令人振奋。

sentences.en: That's how she felt at a recent show.
sentences.zh: 这就是她在最近一场演出中的感受。

sentences.en: There's one thing I did.
sentences.zh: 我做了一件事。

sentences.en: I was like a slug on stage.
sentences.zh: 我在台上像条鼻涕虫一样。

sentences.en: I, like, got on the floor and I, like, acted like a slug.
sentences.zh: 我趴在地板上，像鼻涕虫一样蠕动。

sentences.en: I inchwormed across the stage.
sentences.zh: 我像尺蠖一样爬过了舞台。

sentences.en: Her fellow actors lit up.
sentences.zh: 她的搭档们都兴奋起来了。

sentences.en: The audience exploded in laughter.
sentences.zh: 观众爆发出阵阵笑声。

sentences.en: When Morgan walked out of the theater that night, she was practically bursting.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上摩根走出剧院时，整个人几乎要飘起来了。

sentences.en: I just needed to do something with my energy.
sentences.zh: 我只是需要找个地方发泄一下精力。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't want to just go home and, like, go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不想直接回家睡觉。

sentences.en: Just then...
sentences.zh: 就在那时……

sentences.en: This guy, like, walked out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 这个家伙突然冒了出来。

sentences.en: He was carrying a tripod and a bunch of other stuff.
sentences.zh: 他带着一个三脚架和一堆其他东西。

sentences.en: Like a sack with stuff in it.
sentences.zh: 就像一个装满东西的袋子。

sentences.en: And he was just like, does anybody want to buy this tripod?
sentences.zh: 他直接问，有人想买这个三脚架吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, I want to buy this tripod.
sentences.zh: 我说，好啊，我想买这个三脚架。

sentences.en: I think I could get a lot of use out of a tripod.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我能用得上三脚架。

sentences.en: I was like, how much?
sentences.zh: 我问，多少钱？

sentences.en: And he said, $25.
sentences.zh: 他说，25美元。

sentences.en: And also, I'm going to give you this $50 Amazon gift card.
sentences.zh: 而且，我还要送你这张50美元的亚马逊礼品卡。

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, a tripod and a $50 Amazon gift card for $25?
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，一个三脚架加一张50美元的亚马逊礼品卡只要25美元？

sentences.en: Wow, this guy is so cool.
sentences.zh: 哇，这家伙太酷了。

sentences.en: I'm totally going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我一定要买。

sentences.en: The high she felt from inchwarming across the stage just got even higher.
sentences.zh: 她在舞台上表演带来的兴奋感又更上一层楼了。

sentences.en: Morgan walked with a guy to an ATM.
sentences.zh: 摩根陪那个人走到自动取款机前。

sentences.en: I got my money in 20s.
sentences.zh: 我取出来的钱都是20美元面值的。

sentences.en: So I had to either give him $20 or $40.
sentences.zh: 所以我只能给他20美元或40美元。

sentences.en: She asked if she could give him $20 rather than the full $25.
sentences.zh: 她问能不能只给他20美元，而不是全额的25美元。

sentences.en: He was like, you give me whatever you want to give me.
sentences.zh: 他说，你想给多少就给多少。

sentences.en: And I was like, you're so cool.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，你人真好。

sentences.en: I'm going to give you $40.
sentences.zh: 我要给你40美元。

sentences.en: And I gave him $40.
sentences.zh: 于是我给了他40美元。

sentences.en: And then he gave me like a shoebox full of other random things.
sentences.zh: 然后他给了我一个装满各种杂物的鞋盒。

sentences.en: And I was like, he's so cool.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，他真是太酷了。

sentences.en: Morgan felt like she had hit the jackpot.
sentences.zh: 摩根觉得自己中了大奖。

sentences.en: There was a loofah in there.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个沐浴球。

sentences.en: There was a bunch of pens.
sentences.zh: 还有一堆笔。

sentences.en: And I got really excited about the pens because, I don't know, I just love pens.
sentences.zh: 我对那些笔感到非常兴奋，因为，我也不知道，我就是喜欢笔。

sentences.en: There's, like, stress balls in there.
sentences.zh: 里面还有压力球之类的东西。

sentences.en: There was, like, a diamond cleaner.
sentences.zh: 还有一个钻石清洁器。

sentences.en: I've never heard of a diamond cleaner before, but it's got, like, bristles at the end and, like, this juice on the inside.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没听说过钻石清洁器，但它末端有刷毛，里面还有清洁液。

sentences.en: Um, what else is in there?
sentences.zh: 嗯，里面还有什么？

sentences.en: Arts and craft supplies.
sentences.zh: 手工艺术品材料。

sentences.en: And you also threw in a pair of women's shoes.
sentences.zh: 他还顺手塞进了一双女鞋。

sentences.en: They weren't my size, but I was like, I could sell those.
sentences.zh: 虽然尺码不对，但我当时想，我可以把它们卖掉。

sentences.en: This is awesome.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Morgan couldn't wait to show her roommates the loot.
sentences.zh: 摩根迫不及待地想向室友展示她的战利品。

sentences.en: She burst into her apartment and told them about her unbelievable good fortune.
sentences.zh: 她冲进公寓，告诉她们自己不可思议的好运。

sentences.en: They were like, what is wrong with you?
sentences.zh: 她们问，你到底怎么了？

sentences.en: They were like, okay, what this guy did is he took this stuff out of cars that weren't locked, and then he sold it to you for money.
sentences.zh: 她们说，好吧，这家伙做的事就是从没锁的车里偷了这些东西，然后卖给你换钱。

sentences.en: And slowly, like, my universe just, like, unraveled.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，我的世界观崩塌了。

sentences.en: And I was like, no!
sentences.zh: 我当时想，不！

sentences.en: I just bought a bunch of stolen stuff.
sentences.zh: 我竟然买了一堆赃物。

sentences.en: Why did Morgan, who prides herself on being able to read subtext and situations,
sentences.zh: 为什么以能读懂潜台词和局势而自豪的摩根，

sentences.en: fail to see what seemed obvious to her friends?
sentences.zh: 却没能看出在朋友眼中显而易见的事实？

sentences.en: I like to think of myself as like a pretty logical person.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为自己是个相当理性的人。

sentences.en: But in that moment, I didn't have any logic.
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，我完全失去了理智。

sentences.en: Like, I wasn't questioning the situation.
sentences.zh: 我根本没有质疑那个情况。

sentences.en: I was just being super impulsive.
sentences.zh: 我只是表现得超级冲动。

sentences.en: And so in that way, I think I was being a pretty different person.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度看，我觉得自己当时完全变成了另一个人。

sentences.en: It's as if there are two people within Morgan, and neither understands the other.
sentences.zh: 就好像摩根体内住着两个人，而且谁也不理解谁。

sentences.en: Logical Morgan thinks impulsive Morgan made a glaring mistake.
sentences.zh: 理性的摩根认为冲动的摩根犯了一个明显的错误。

sentences.en: But impulsive Morgan is just as bewildered by logical Morgan.
sentences.zh: 但冲动的摩根对理性的摩根也同样感到困惑。

sentences.en: Who would pass up a deal like this?
sentences.zh: 谁会错过这样的交易呢？

sentences.en: George Lowenstein understands what Morgan was experiencing.
sentences.zh: 乔治·洛温斯坦理解摩根当时的经历。

sentences.en: George lives in the Pittsburgh area, which is home to some of the steepest hills in America.
sentences.zh: 乔治住在匹兹堡地区，那里有美国最陡峭的一些山坡。

sentences.en: He used to run those hills every week with his friend Jules.
sentences.zh: 他过去每周都会和朋友朱尔斯一起跑那些山坡。

sentences.en: We would get absolutely exhausted on the way up,
sentences.zh: 我们在上坡时会精疲力竭，

sentences.en: and we'd kind of be egging one another on and be feeling very, very miserable.
sentences.zh: 我们会互相怂恿，感觉非常非常痛苦。

sentences.en: On the way up to the peak, all he could think of was the pain.
sentences.zh: 在爬向顶峰的过程中，他满脑子想的都是痛苦。

sentences.en: But moments later...
sentences.zh: 但片刻之后……

sentences.en: It was all forgotten within maybe 10, 20 seconds.
sentences.zh: 这一切在10到20秒内就被遗忘了。

sentences.en: The more George thought about it, the more it seemed like a puzzle.
sentences.zh: 乔治越想越觉得这是一个谜。

sentences.en: As he was climbing the hill, the idea of relief was inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 当他爬坡时，解脱的想法是不可想象的。

sentences.en: The pain felt endless.
sentences.zh: 痛苦感觉永无止境。

sentences.en: But the moment he crested the hill, the pain faded so quickly that in his memory, it hadn't been so bad.
sentences.zh: 但当他到达山顶的那一刻，痛苦消退得如此之快，以至于在他的记忆中，那并没有那么糟糕。

sentences.en: A few days later, he would lace up his shoes and go running with Jules again.
sentences.zh: 几天后，他会再次系好鞋带，和朱尔斯一起去跑步。

sentences.en: It occurred to George that this gap in perception was psychologically important and applied to more than just the pain of running.
sentences.zh: 乔治意识到，这种感知上的差距在心理学上很重要，而且不仅仅适用于跑步的痛苦。

sentences.en: I realize that when you're not in pain or cold or experiencing a powerful emotion like anger or fear,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，当你没有感到痛苦、寒冷，或者没有经历愤怒或恐惧等强烈情绪时，

sentences.en: it's very difficult to imagine yourself in that situation.
sentences.zh: 很难想象自己处于那种境地。

sentences.en: There is a reason this happens.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生是有原因的。

sentences.en: Emotions completely transform us as people.
sentences.zh: 情绪会彻底改变我们作为人的状态。

sentences.en: So when we're in one emotional state, it's as if we're a different person than we are when we're in a different emotional state.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们处于一种情绪状态时，就好像我们与处于另一种情绪状态时是不同的人。

sentences.en: George has thought about this phenomenon a lot.
sentences.zh: 乔治对这种现象思考了很多。

sentences.en: As a professor of psychology and economics at Carnegie Mellon University,
sentences.zh: 作为卡内基梅隆大学的心理学和经济学教授，

sentences.en: he has conducted dozens of studies to understand how our emotional states affect us.
sentences.zh: 他进行了数十项研究，以了解我们的情绪状态如何影响我们。

sentences.en: One of his earliest studies involved ice water.
sentences.zh: 他最早的研究之一涉及冰水。

sentences.en: My colleague wanted to be the guinea pig for the studies,
sentences.zh: 我的同事想成为研究的实验对象，

sentences.en: and you're supposed to put your hand in the cold water for like a minute.
sentences.zh: 你需要把手放在冷水里大约一分钟。

sentences.en: He put his hand in the cold water, and 20 seconds later, he pulled it out.
sentences.zh: 他把手放进冷水里，20秒后就抽了出来。

sentences.en: And then a minute later, he said, that's ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 一分钟后，他说，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: I can do it, because he couldn't remember the pain anymore.
sentences.zh: 我能做到，因为他已经记不住那种痛苦了。

sentences.en: Expecting fully that he would be able to sustain the minute in the cold water.
sentences.zh: 他完全相信自己能够坚持在冷水中待上一分钟。

sentences.en: And then about 20 seconds later, he pulled his hand out again.
sentences.zh: 然后大约20秒后，他又把手抽了出来。

sentences.en: It was just like what George experienced on his runs.
sentences.zh: 这就像乔治在跑步时的经历一样。

sentences.en: As soon as his colleague pulled his hand out of the freezing water,
sentences.zh: 当他的同事把手从冰冷的水中抽出来时，

sentences.en: it was like he was struck with amnesia.
sentences.zh: 就像患上了失忆症一样。

sentences.en: George came up with a name for what was happening.
sentences.zh: 乔治为这种现象起了一个名字。

sentences.en: The hot, cold, empathy gap.
sentences.zh: “冷热同理心差距”。

sentences.en: Usually, when we think about empathy, we think about how we relate to other people.
sentences.zh: 通常，当我们想到同理心时，我们想到的是我们如何与他人产生共鸣。

sentences.en: George's insight is that we regularly lack empathy for ourselves when we are in a different
sentences.zh: 乔治的见解是，当我们处于不同的情绪状态时，我们经常对自己缺乏同理心。

sentences.en: emotional state.
sentences.zh: 情绪状态。

sentences.en: When we're angry, we cannot imagine being calm.
sentences.zh: 当我们愤怒时，我们无法想象自己会冷静。

sentences.en: When we are tranquil,
sentences.zh: 当我们平静时，

sentences.en: it's hard to imagine being so angry that we could hurt someone.
sentences.zh: 很难想象自己会愤怒到伤害他人。

sentences.en: The hot-cold empathy gap
sentences.zh: “冷热共情差距”

sentences.en: can also be caused by physiological states.
sentences.zh: 也可能由生理状态引起。

sentences.en: When we are really hungry, all our resolutions about
sentences.zh: 当我们极度饥饿时，所有关于

sentences.en: healthy eating evaporate.
sentences.zh: 健康饮食的决心都会烟消云散。

sentences.en: When we are full, it's easy to forget what it felt like to be hungry.
sentences.zh: 当我们吃饱时，很容易忘记饥饿时的感觉。

sentences.en: We imagine that we will stick to salads the next day.
sentences.zh: 我们以为第二天自己会坚持吃沙拉。

sentences.en: The hot and cold in the hot-cold empathy gap
sentences.zh: “冷热共情差距”中的“冷”与“热”

sentences.en: are a shorthand.
sentences.zh: 是一种简略的说法。

sentences.en: They describe strong emotional and physiological states.
sentences.zh: 它们描述的是强烈的情绪和生理状态。

sentences.en: When we're in a cold
sentences.zh: 当我们处于“冷”

sentences.en: state, we're logical, deliberate.
sentences.zh: 状态时，我们是理性的、深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: When we're in a hot state, our emotions overtake us.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于“热”状态时，情绪会占据上风。

sentences.en: Morgan Smalley was in a hot state when a young man sold her a sack of random stuff.
sentences.zh: 摩根·斯莫利（Morgan Smalley）在被一个年轻人兜售一袋杂物时，就处于一种“热”状态。

sentences.en: In her excitement, her skepticism failed to kick in.
sentences.zh: 在兴奋之下，她的怀疑心理完全没起作用。

sentences.en: Another familiar hot state?
sentences.zh: 另一种常见的“热”状态是什么？

sentences.en: Sexual arousal.
sentences.zh: 性唤起。

sentences.en: Can I talk about that on NPR?
sentences.zh: 我能在美国国家公共电台（NPR）上谈论这个吗？

sentences.en: Like, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 呃，我不知道。

sentences.en: The answer is yes.

sentences.zh: 在研究的第二部分，朱莉设计了一个实验，来测试女性是否真的会做她们预想中会做的事。

sentences.en: We had 50 women who were applying for a job.
sentences.zh: 我们找了50名正在申请工作的女性。

sentences.en: The job was a research assistant in a lab.
sentences.zh: 这份工作是实验室的研究助理。

sentences.en: The women would come into the interview, and we had covert cameras set up.
sentences.zh: 女性们来参加面试，我们安装了隐蔽摄像头。

sentences.en: Their interviewer was a man in his mid-30s.
sentences.zh: 面试官是一名30多岁的男性。

sentences.en: He asked those three questions.
sentences.zh: 他问了那三个问题。

sentences.en: The same three questions from the first phase of the study.
sentences.zh: 与研究第一阶段完全相同的三个问题。

sentences.en: Do you have a boyfriend?
sentences.zh: 你有男朋友吗？

sentences.en: Do people find you desirable?
sentences.zh: 别人觉得你有魅力吗？

sentences.en: Do you think it's important for women to wear bras to work?
sentences.zh: 你认为女性上班穿胸罩重要吗？

sentences.en: What was different here was that the women weren't imagining a job interview.
sentences.zh: 这里不同的是，这些女性并不是在想象面试场景。

sentences.en: They were in a job interview, or so they believed.
sentences.zh: 她们正身处面试中，或者说她们是这么认为的。

sentences.en: So how did they react?
sentences.zh: 那么她们是如何反应的呢？

sentences.en: Did 90% respond assertively?
sentences.zh: 有90%的人坚定地回应了吗？

sentences.en: Tell the interviewer off?
sentences.zh: 斥责面试官了吗？

sentences.en: Slap him and walk out?
sentences.zh: 扇他一巴掌然后走人了吗？

sentences.en: Nobody left.
sentences.zh: 没有人离开。

sentences.en: Every single person answered every single question.
sentences.zh: 每个人都回答了每一个问题。

sentences.en: Some women did speak up, but generally not until the end of the interview.
sentences.zh: 有些女性确实开口说了话，但通常要等到面试快结束时才说。

sentences.en: 36% of the participants at that point said very politely,
sentences.zh: 当时有36%的参与者非常有礼貌地说：

sentences.en: yeah, I was just wondering, you know, why did you ask about me being desirable?
sentences.zh: 那个，我只是想问一下，你为什么要问我是否有魅力？

sentences.en: There was another important difference between the women's responses in the two parts of the study.
sentences.zh: 在研究的两个部分中，女性的反应还有另一个重要的区别。

sentences.en: So you remember in the anticipated study, most women responded that they'd be angry, very few fearful.
sentences.zh: 还记得在预想研究中，大多数女性说她们会感到愤怒，很少感到恐惧。

sentences.en: And it was the flip in this study.
sentences.zh: 但在这次研究中情况完全反过来了。

sentences.en: So we found that many women reported feeling afraid in that situation, and anger was not very much reported.
sentences.zh: 我们发现许多女性报告说在那样的情境下感到害怕，而愤怒的报告则很少。

sentences.en: While the women who imagined being sexually harassed thought they'd be angry and that anger would propel them to act,
sentences.zh: 虽然那些想象自己遭遇性骚扰的女性认为自己会愤怒，并且愤怒会促使她们采取行动，

sentences.en: women who were face-to-face with a harasser, in fact, experienced fear.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，与骚扰者面对面的女性感受到的却是恐惧。

sentences.en: There's clearly an aspect of the study that should make you uneasy.
sentences.zh: 这项研究显然有一个方面会让你感到不安。

sentences.en: Researchers brought in unsuspecting women for what they thought were job interviews
sentences.zh: 研究人员把毫无防备的女性带进来，让她们以为是去面试，

sentences.en: and then subjected them to harassment to see how they would behave.
sentences.zh: 然后让她们遭受骚扰，看看她们会有什么表现。

sentences.en: Julie went through rigorous ethical clearance to conduct the study.
sentences.zh: 朱莉通过了严格的伦理审查才进行这项研究。

sentences.en: After it was over, she debriefed the volunteers
sentences.zh: 结束后，她向志愿者说明了情况，

sentences.en: and gave them the option of pulling their data.
sentences.zh: 并让她们选择是否撤回自己的数据。

sentences.en: What explains the enormous gap between what women think they do
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了女性认为自己会怎么做，

sentences.en: and what they actually do?
sentences.zh: 与她们实际会怎么做之间存在巨大的鸿沟？

sentences.en: When we're asked to anticipate how we would respond, we don't take into account, one, how our emotional state in that moment, especially if it's a highly charged moment,
sentences.zh: 当我们被要求预想自己会如何应对时，我们没有考虑到，第一，我们在那一刻的情绪状态，尤其是在这种高度紧张的时刻，

sentences.en: will impact our behavior.
sentences.zh: 会如何影响我们的行为。

sentences.en: We're not thinking about how being in a hot state might affect us.
sentences.zh: 我们没有考虑到处于“热状态”下会如何影响我们。

sentences.en: We also don't understand very well, I think, the strength of the situation and just what would be the cost of leaving.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们也不太理解情境的力量，以及离开的代价究竟是什么。

sentences.en: How would people perceive us?
sentences.zh: 别人会怎么看我们？

sentences.en: They're not thinking about how they're going to be feeling.
sentences.zh: 她们没有考虑到自己届时会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: They're not thinking about even really the other people in the situation.
sentences.zh: 她们甚至没有真正考虑到情境中的其他人。

sentences.en: They're just thinking about what would they do.
sentences.zh: 她们只是在想自己会怎么做。

sentences.en: It's like wanting to build a house and showing up to the groundbreaking with only a sketch,
sentences.zh: 这就像想要盖一栋房子，却只带着一张草图去参加奠基仪式，

sentences.en: a sketch that doesn't take into consideration any of the context or any of the obstacles,
sentences.zh: 那张草图没有考虑到任何背景或障碍，

sentences.en: like the engineering requirements or the zoning laws or the funding.
sentences.zh: 比如工程要求、分区法或资金问题。

sentences.en: If you had outlined the scenario that Nina Fuller found herself in,
sentences.zh: 如果你向妮娜·富勒描述她所处的那种情境，

sentences.en: she would have told you ahead of time that she would have walked out of the massage parlor.
sentences.zh: 她会提前告诉你，她会直接走出那家按摩店。

sentences.en: What she would not have been able to factor into her thinking was the change in her emotional state,
sentences.zh: 她无法预料到的是她情绪状态的变化，

sentences.en: her surprise, her fear, her shock, and how those emotions might have affected her ability to act.
sentences.zh: 她的惊讶、恐惧、震惊，以及这些情绪如何影响了她的行动能力。

sentences.en: You know, if you were to think about that, you would say, oh, I'd be so mad.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你去想这件事，你会说，哦，我会非常生气。

sentences.en: I'd be so mad at that guy.
sentences.zh: 我会对那个家伙非常生气。

sentences.en: Like, what's he thinking?
sentences.zh: 心想，他在想什么？

sentences.en: But in actuality, she's alone in a room with a guy.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，她独自和那个男人待在一个房间里。

sentences.en: She doesn't really know, like, what this whole situation is,
sentences.zh: 她并不真正知道整个情况是怎么回事，

sentences.en: except that she's been hired to give a massage and she has no experience doing that.
sentences.zh: 只知道自己被雇来做按摩，而且她对此毫无经验。

sentences.en: And she's probably feeling afraid.
sentences.zh: 她可能感到很害怕。

sentences.en: She's not feeling angry.
sentences.zh: 她并没有感到愤怒。

sentences.en: One thing to confront someone turns out to be just one step in actually confronting someone.
sentences.zh: 对抗某人这件事，其实只是真正对抗某人的第一步。

sentences.en: And it is not even the first step.
sentences.zh: 甚至连第一步都算不上。

sentences.en: First, you have to interpret that something happened that actually is sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 首先，你必须解读出发生的事情确实是性骚扰。

sentences.en: Then you have to interpret the event as confrontation worthy.
sentences.zh: 然后，你必须将该事件解读为值得对抗的。

sentences.en: So is this event worthy of confrontation or is it really not that big of a deal?
sentences.zh: 所以，这件事值得对抗吗？还是说其实没那么严重？

sentences.en: Then you have to actually take responsibility to confront.
sentences.zh: 然后，你必须真正承担起对抗的责任。

sentences.en: Then you have to decide or you have to come up with different response options.
sentences.zh: 接着，你必须决定或想出不同的应对方案。

sentences.en: What am I actually going to do?
sentences.zh: 我到底该怎么做？

sentences.en: And then you actually have to do it.
sentences.zh: 最后，你必须真正付诸行动。

sentences.en: So when most people think about confrontation, they think about it being just one step.
sentences.zh: 所以，当大多数人想到对抗时，他们认为这只是一步。

sentences.en: You know, I'm either going to confront or I'm not going to confront.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要么我要么对抗，要么我不对抗。

sentences.en: I'm going to ask someone to make it stop or I won't.
sentences.zh: 我要么要求对方停止，要么就不要求。

sentences.en: But in actuality, it's five pretty separate big steps that you have to take to be able to confront at the end.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，要实现最终的对抗，你必须完成五个相当独立的大步骤。

sentences.en: Listening to George Loewenstein and Julie Woodzica made me think about sexual harassment prevention prograMs.
sentences.zh: 听了乔治·洛温斯坦和朱莉·伍兹卡的研究，我开始思考性骚扰预防项目。

sentences.en: Many of these programs try to address the abuse of power that drives so much sexual harassment.
sentences.zh: 许多这类项目试图解决导致大量性骚扰的权力滥用问题。

sentences.en: But many also ignore the hot-cold empathy gap.
sentences.zh: 但许多项目也忽视了“热-冷同理心差距”。

sentences.en: The advice given to participants is respect other people's boundaries.
sentences.zh: 给参与者的建议是尊重他人的界限。

sentences.en: Don't say and do things you would later regret.
sentences.zh: 不要说或做你以后会后悔的事情。

sentences.en: People listening might think, sure, that's easy.
sentences.zh: 听众可能会想，当然，这很简单。

sentences.en: They're in a cold state, and they can't imagine how sexual arousal can turn them into the kind of people who violate boundaries or make colleagues uneasy.
sentences.zh: 他们处于“冷状态”，无法想象性冲动如何能让他们变成那种侵犯界限或让同事感到不安的人。

sentences.en: The training programs also tell potential victims and bystanders, don't be silent.
sentences.zh: 培训项目也告诉潜在的受害者和旁观者，不要保持沉默。

sentences.en: Report probleMs. If you see something, say something.
sentences.zh: 报告问题。如果你看到了什么，就说出来。

sentences.en: People listening think, of course I would never be silent in a situation like that.
sentences.zh: 听众心想，我当然绝不会在那种情况下保持沉默。

sentences.en: They go back to their desks with the feeling
sentences.zh: 他们回到办公桌前，感觉

sentences.en: that they know exactly how they would act in these situations.
sentences.zh: 自己完全知道在这些情况下该如何行动。

sentences.en: The hot-cold empathy gap doesn't just make us draw the wrong conclusions
sentences.zh: “热-冷同理心差距”不仅让我们对自己的行为和动机

sentences.en: about our actions and motivations.
sentences.zh: 得出错误的结论。

sentences.en: It can make us unfairly judgmental toward others.
sentences.zh: 它还会让我们对他人的评价有失公允。

sentences.en: We hear what someone else did, someone like Anita Hill,
sentences.zh: 我们听到别人做了什么，比如安妮塔·希尔，

sentences.en: and think, I would never have done that.
sentences.zh: 就会想，我绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: I would have acted differently.
sentences.zh: 我会采取不同的行动。

sentences.en: It's very difficult to make sense of other people's behavior,
sentences.zh: 要理解他人的行为非常困难，

sentences.en: people who are acting under the influence of emotions that you're not experiencing.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些在某种你并未经历的情绪影响下做出行为的人。

sentences.en: George Loewenstein says our unrealistic sense of how we would act
sentences.zh: 乔治·洛温斯坦说，我们对自己会如何行动的不切实际的认知，

sentences.en: is at the root of our failure to understand others.
sentences.zh: 是我们无法理解他人的根源。

sentences.en: When we assess whether another person's actions are reasonable,
sentences.zh: 当我们评估他人的行为是否合理时，

sentences.en: we first imagine how we would behave in that situation.
sentences.zh: 我们首先想象的是自己在那种情况下会如何表现。

sentences.en: The problem is our perceptions are out of whack with reality.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，我们的感知与现实脱节了。

sentences.en: We think we'd be able to control an addiction or slog through pain
sentences.zh: 我们以为自己能够控制瘾头，或者能够忍受痛苦。

sentences.en: or confront a harasser.
sentences.zh: 或者去对抗骚扰者。

sentences.en: When we come back,
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，

sentences.en: we may never be able to avoid the hot-cold empathy gap,
sentences.zh: 我们或许永远无法避免“冷热共情差距”，

sentences.en: but there are ways to compensate for it.
sentences.zh: 但有一些方法可以弥补它。

sentences.en: I was like, I don't know if this is worth it.
sentences.zh: 我当时心想，不知道这是否值得。

sentences.en: You know, my legs hurt, my body hurts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的腿很痛，身体也很痛。

sentences.en: I just want to go home and go to sleep right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在只想回家睡觉。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam,
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，

sentences.en: and you're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: All of us see and do things
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都会看到并做出一些

sentences.en: we would never anticipate saying and doing.
sentences.zh: 我们从未预料到自己会说或做的事情。

sentences.en: When we are in the thrall of intense emotions, we are impulsive when we should be cautious.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于强烈情绪的支配下时，本该谨慎的我们却变得冲动。

sentences.en: We freeze when we think we will be brave.
sentences.zh: 我们本以为自己会很勇敢，结果却僵住了。

sentences.en: When we look back on our behavior, we are often baffled because we have forgotten how
sentences.zh: 当我们回顾自己的行为时，往往会感到困惑，因为我们已经忘记了

sentences.en: we felt in the heat of the moment.
sentences.zh: 自己在当时那种冲动状态下的感受。

sentences.en: Psychologist George Lowenstein calls this an empathy gap.
sentences.zh: 心理学家乔治·洛温斯坦称之为“共情差距”。

sentences.en: We often can't relate to the other person we become in a different emotional state.
sentences.zh: 我们往往无法理解处于不同情绪状态下的另一个自己。

sentences.en: We might think that one way to bridge this gap is to see how we behave when we are in the grip of an intense emotion.
sentences.zh: 我们可能认为，弥合这一差距的方法之一，就是看看我们在处于强烈情绪时是如何表现的。

sentences.en: Surely, after we see how we act in one of these emotional states, we won't be as naive the next time around.
sentences.zh: 当然，在见识过自己在某种情绪状态下的表现后，下一次我们应该就不会那么天真了。

sentences.en: We think experience functions like a powerful vaccine, once inoculated, forever protected.
sentences.zh: 我们认为经验就像一种强效疫苗，一旦接种，便能终身免疫。

sentences.en: All my research suggests that experiencing something yourself does not provide any inoculation against the empathy gap.
sentences.zh: 但我所有的研究都表明，亲身经历并不能提供任何针对共情差距的免疫力。

sentences.en: If experience was a simple fix, George's colleague wouldn't have believed he'd be able to keep his hand in ice water the second time around.
sentences.zh: 如果经验能简单解决问题，乔治的同事就不会相信自己第二次还能把手放在冰水里。

sentences.en: Irene would not have had unprotected sex with a no underwear, no condoms guy twice.
sentences.zh: 艾琳也不会两次与一个不穿内裤、不戴避孕套的男人发生无保护性行为。

sentences.en: Most of us don't even get to the point where we recognize how different our hot and cold selves are.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人甚至还没意识到自己的“热状态”和“冷状态”有多么不同。

sentences.en: But even if we did, that would not be enough to change our behavior.
sentences.zh: 但即使意识到了，也不足以改变我们的行为。

sentences.en: We have to develop the muscle memory to override our instincts in those states.
sentences.zh: 我们必须培养肌肉记忆，以便在那些状态下超越本能。

sentences.en: George has found an effective way to do so.
sentences.zh: 乔治发现了一种有效的方法。

sentences.en: Training.
sentences.zh: 训练。

sentences.en: Well, I think what training often does is it diminishes the hot state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为训练通常起到的作用是削弱“热状态”。

sentences.en: So, for example, when I started out in public speaking,
sentences.zh: 例如，当我刚开始公开演讲时，

sentences.en: I found it very, very painful, anxiety-making.
sentences.zh: 我发现这非常非常痛苦，令人焦虑。

sentences.en: I would get dry mouth, things like that.
sentences.zh: 我会口干舌燥，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And then the more I did it, the less miserable I found it.
sentences.zh: 后来做得越多，我发现它就越没那么痛苦。

sentences.en: I still find radio interviews totally miserable.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然觉得广播采访非常痛苦。

sentences.en: There's an entire American institution devoted to bridging the hot-cold empathy gap
sentences.zh: 美国有一个专门致力于弥合“冷热共情差距”的机构，

sentences.en: in situations far more physically taxing than a radio interview.
sentences.zh: 其环境比广播采访要艰苦得多。

sentences.en: It's the Army.
sentences.zh: 那就是陆军。

sentences.en: Military leaders have long understood that there is a way to get soldiers to perform well in battle,
sentences.zh: 军事领导人早就明白，有一种方法可以让士兵在战斗中表现出色，

sentences.en: Put them in heart states and teach them, through repetition, to stifle their natural impulses.
sentences.zh: 那就是让他们进入“热状态”，并通过重复训练，教他们抑制自己的自然冲动。

sentences.en: My name is Anastasia Fish.
sentences.zh: 我叫阿纳斯塔西娅·菲什。

sentences.en: I'm a second lieutenant in the United States Army, and I'm an armor officer.
sentences.zh: 我是美国陆军的一名少尉，也是一名装甲军官。

sentences.en: On a February morning in 2019, Anastasia had her roommate drive her to Camp Darby in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 2019年2月的一个早晨，阿纳斯塔西娅让室友开车送她去佐治亚州的达比营。

sentences.en: As they approached the camp, they passed a black and yellow sign that Anastasia had seen her friends pose in front of in their Instagram photos.
sentences.zh: 当他们接近营地时，经过了一个黑黄相间的标志，阿纳斯塔西娅曾在朋友们的Instagram照片中看到过他们站在这个标志前摆姿势。

sentences.en: The sign read,
sentences.zh: 标志上写着：

sentences.en: Not for the weak or fainthearted.
sentences.zh: 弱者或胆小者勿入。

sentences.en: It's a warning and a boast for Army Ranger School.
sentences.zh: 这是对陆军游骑兵学校的警告和夸耀。

sentences.en: The school puts recruits through a grueling training program.
sentences.zh: 该学校让新兵经历极其严苛的训练计划。

sentences.en: Graduates often go on to elite units and important assignments.
sentences.zh: 毕业生通常会进入精英部队并担任重要职务。

sentences.en: On the first full day of training, Anastasia says she had to take a teSt.
sentences.zh: 在训练的第一整天，阿纳斯塔西娅说她必须参加测试。

sentences.en: You have two minutes to do 49 push-ups.
sentences.zh: 两分钟内要做49个俯卧撑。

sentences.en: You have two minutes to do 59 sit-ups.
sentences.zh: 两分钟内要做59个仰卧起坐。

sentences.en: You have 40 minutes to run five miles, and then you have to do six pull-ups right afterwards.
sentences.zh: 40分钟内跑完五英里，之后紧接着要做6个引体向上。

sentences.en: In the weeks that followed, Anastasia had to drop from a rope into cold water and swim,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，阿纳斯塔西娅必须穿着全套制服，

sentences.en: wearing her full uniform.
sentences.zh: 从绳子上跳入冷水中游泳。

sentences.en: She was kept awake for hours on end.
sentences.zh: 她连续几个小时被剥夺睡眠。

sentences.en: She recalls a stretch of nine days where she only got 10 hours of sleep total.
sentences.zh: 她回忆起有一段长达九天的日子，总共只睡了10个小时。

sentences.en: She was constantly distracted by hunger.
sentences.zh: 她一直受到饥饿的干扰。

sentences.en: We looked at some videos online of Army Ranger training.
sentences.zh: 我们在网上看了一些陆军游骑兵训练的视频。

sentences.en: It's hard to believe human beings could survive those challenges.
sentences.zh: 很难相信人类能挺过这些挑战。

sentences.en: All this suffering had a purpose, to put trainees like Anastasia into a heart state,
sentences.zh: 所有这些痛苦都是有目的的，就是为了让像阿纳斯塔西娅这样的学员进入“热状态”，

sentences.en: even though her instructors called it something else.
sentences.zh: 尽管她的教官们用了别的称呼。

sentences.en: As far as ranger school goes, they like to use the term stress inoculation.
sentences.zh: 就游骑兵学校而言，他们喜欢用“压力接种”这个词。

sentences.en: So they create a lot of stress, and then they teach you how to live in that and how to cope with it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们制造大量的压力，然后教你如何在这种压力下生活，如何应对它。

sentences.en: The stressors were both physical and psychological.
sentences.zh: 这些压力源既有生理上的，也有心理上的。

sentences.en: She was asked to oversee a dozen people in a simulated military mission.
sentences.zh: 她被要求在一次模拟军事任务中监督十几个人。

sentences.en: She had to organize a surprise attack.
sentences.zh: 她必须组织一次突袭。

sentences.en: At first, I was very nervous about it.
sentences.zh: 起初，我对此感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: She had to force herself to calm down and think through what needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 她必须强迫自己冷静下来，思考需要完成的事情。

sentences.en: I kind of learned how to take pieces of the task and effectively execute the pieces.
sentences.zh: 我学会了如何把任务拆解成小块，并有效地执行这些小块。

sentences.en: And I could look at basically a 5-meter target instead of a 50-meter target.
sentences.zh: 我可以把目光放在5米的目标上，而不是50米的目标上。

sentences.en: And I could take my little 5-meter targets and I could very, very easily accomplish those tasks.
sentences.zh: 我可以处理好我的那些5米小目标，并且非常非常轻松地完成这些任务。

sentences.en: She used simple tools, a notebook and pen, and made checklists.
sentences.zh: 她使用了简单的工具，笔记本和笔，并制作了清单。

sentences.en: And then any time that I'd start to feel kind of panicked or anxious because I was like,
sentences.zh: 每当我觉得有点恐慌或焦虑时，因为我心想，

sentences.en: things aren't happening fast enough because everyone's tired,
sentences.zh: 事情进展得不够快，因为每个人都很累，

sentences.en: or things aren't happening fast enough because people are distracted,
sentences.zh: 或者事情进展得不够快，因为人们注意力不集中，

sentences.en: I was able to look at my list and think about the things that I could check off
sentences.zh: 我就能看看我的清单，想想我可以勾掉的事情，

sentences.en: or things that were going to be checked off soon.
sentences.zh: 或者很快就能勾掉的事情。

sentences.en: And that really actually helped me relax because I knew that things were getting done.
sentences.zh: 这实际上真的帮我放松了下来，因为我知道事情正在完成。

sentences.en: and the more check marks I had on my list, the better I knew I was doing.
sentences.zh: 而且清单上的勾号越多，我就越清楚自己做得越好。

sentences.en: Anastasia learned to control her behavior in different heart states.
sentences.zh: 阿纳斯塔西娅学会了在不同的“热状态”下控制自己的行为。

sentences.en: But it took weeks of round-the-clock training to get to that point.
sentences.zh: 但为了达到这一点，她经历了数周全天候的训练。

sentences.en: Few of us could handle what it takes to get our hungry, achy, exhausted selves
sentences.zh: 我们很少有人能处理好如何让饥饿、疼痛、疲惫的自己，

sentences.en: to behave like our cold state selves.
sentences.zh: 表现得像处于“冷状态”下的自己那样。

sentences.en: But not all challenges involve leading a team into battle.
sentences.zh: 但并非所有的挑战都涉及带领团队投入战斗。

sentences.en: In civilian life, there can be less daunting ways
sentences.zh: 在平民生活中，也有一些不那么令人生畏的方法，

sentences.en: to train yourself to respond to everyday challenges.
sentences.zh: 可以训练自己去应对日常挑战。

sentences.en: Self-defense classes are designed to teach you
sentences.zh: 自卫课程旨在教你，

sentences.en: how to respond if you're attacked.
sentences.zh: 如果受到攻击该如何反应。

sentences.en: Fire drills are designed to teach you
sentences.zh: 消防演习旨在教你，

sentences.en: to keep your head during an emergency.
sentences.zh: 在紧急情况下保持头脑清醒。

sentences.en: Julie Woodzica is developing a training program
sentences.zh: 朱莉·伍兹卡正在开发一个培训项目，

sentences.en: to help women respond to sexist comments and jokes.
sentences.zh: 帮助女性应对性别歧视的言论和笑话。

sentences.en: It's called Fighting Fire with Fire.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“以火攻火”。

sentences.zh: 例如，一个男人讲了一个性别歧视的笑话，

sentences.en: and then the woman says,

sentences.en: wow, still single, huh, Mark?
sentences.zh: 哇，马克，还是单身呢？

sentences.en: Which is funny,
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，

sentences.en: but the guy knows that like oh you know she didn't like that every woman that you talk to can think
sentences.zh: 但那个男人知道，哦，你知道她不喜欢那样。每个你交谈过的女性都能想到，

sentences.en: of a time that they walked away from a situation where something sexist was said and you know 10
sentences.zh: 她们曾离开过某种说了性别歧视言论的场合，你知道，10

sentences.en: minutes later they think of the perfect comeback like oh I wish I had said this and of course in
sentences.zh: 分钟后她们才想到完美的回复，比如，哦，我真希望当时说了这句话。当然，在

sentences.en: the moment you don't think of it so we're thinking if we can have a couple that are kind of in your
sentences.zh: 那一刻你根本想不到。所以我们在想，如果我们能准备几个像是在

sentences.en: back pocket like can you repeat that and hear you over my eyes rolling or just things that are you
sentences.zh: 口袋里备用的回复，比如“你能重复一遍吗？我听着你说话都翻白眼了”，或者只是那些

sentences.en: know, easy to say and would apply to a lot of situations, maybe we can help women to confront
sentences.zh: 你知道，容易说出口且适用于很多情况的话，也许我们就能帮助女性以

sentences.en: in more subtle ways.
sentences.zh: 更微妙的方式进行对抗。

sentences.en: Because it's hard.
sentences.zh: 因为这很难。

sentences.en: It's hard to tell people that they're being sexiSt.
sentences.zh: 告诉别人他们有性别歧视很难。

sentences.en: Julie thinks that in a better world, women wouldn't have this burden of devising comebacks.
sentences.zh: 朱莉认为，在一个更好的世界里，女性不需要背负想出反击话语的负担。

sentences.en: But for the moment, these one-liners give women tools.
sentences.zh: 但目前，这些俏皮话为女性提供了工具。

sentences.en: George Lowenstein says some hot-cold
sentences.zh: 乔治·洛温斯坦说，有些冷热

sentences.en: situations are too challenging for us to manage as individuals.
sentences.zh: 状态下的情况对我们个人来说太难处理了。

sentences.en: I think the solution is good
sentences.zh: 我认为解决方案是好的

sentences.en: public policy.
sentences.zh: 公共政策。

sentences.en: Specifically, he says, public policy should make it easier for people in a hot state
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他说，公共政策应该让处于“热状态”的人更容易

sentences.en: to make the same decisions they would otherwise choose in a cold state.
sentences.zh: 做出他们在“冷状态”下会选择的决定。

sentences.en: Condoms, he says,
sentences.zh: 他说，避孕套

sentences.en: should be quickly and easily accessible.
sentences.zh: 应该能够快速且容易地获得。

sentences.en: So, for example, condoms should be kind of ubiquitously
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，避孕套应该随处

sentences.en: available.
sentences.zh: 可见。

sentences.en: In other cases, George believes that policy should be designed to slow down our actions.
sentences.zh: 在其他情况下，乔治认为政策的设计应该旨在减缓我们的行动。

sentences.en: If I got really angry at someone, I could just go down to Walmart and buy a gun today.
sentences.zh: 如果我真的对某人生气，我今天就可以去沃尔玛买一把枪。

sentences.en: That shouldn't be, you know, that shouldn't be possible.
sentences.zh: 那不应该，你知道，那不应该是可能的。

sentences.en: When you combine the instant availability of guns and empathy gaps, that's a very toxic mixture.
sentences.zh: 当你把枪支的即时可获得性和共情差距结合起来时，那是非常有毒的混合物。

sentences.en: He also sees implications for our criminal justice system,
sentences.zh: 他还看到了这对我们刑事司法系统的影响，

sentences.en: where judges and juries determine how to treat people who have acted in hard states.
sentences.zh: 法官和陪审团在其中决定如何对待那些在“热状态”下行事的人。

sentences.en: Take drug addiction, for example.
sentences.zh: 以药物成瘾为例。

sentences.en: People who have never experienced drug craving,
sentences.zh: 从未经历过毒瘾渴望的人，

sentences.en: they are not going to have any understanding of how powerfully motivating it can be.
sentences.zh: 他们根本无法理解这种渴望的动力有多么强大。

sentences.en: I sometimes ask my students, suppose you were addicted to heroin,
sentences.zh: 我有时会问我的学生，假设你对海洛因上瘾了，

sentences.en: can you imagine ever abandoning your children or stealing from your parents?
sentences.zh: 你能想象自己会抛弃孩子或偷父母的钱吗？

sentences.en: And everyone says, of course, I would never do that.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，当然，我绝不会那样做。

sentences.en: But if they were addicted to heroin, it's very likely that they would do that.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们真的对海洛因上瘾，他们很有可能会那样做。

sentences.en: So in so many of these different situations, like in the criminal justice system,
sentences.zh: 所以在这么多不同的情况下，比如在刑事司法系统中，

sentences.en: it's so easy for people to condemn the behavior of people who are experiencing
sentences.zh: 人们很容易谴责那些正在经历某种状态的人的行为，

sentences.en: states that they themselves are not experiencing when they make the judgment.
sentences.zh: 而他们在做出判断时，自己并没有经历过那种状态。

sentences.en: We might need policy to constrain our decisions,
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要政策来约束我们的决定，

sentences.en: but one thing we can do on our own is to be more compassionate
sentences.zh: 但我们自己能做的一件事，就是在评判他人和自己时，

sentences.en: when we're judging others and ourselves.
sentences.zh: 更加富有同情心。

sentences.en: Nina Fuller, the woman who can't let go of that one night in the massage parlor half a century ago,
sentences.zh: 尼娜·富勒，那个半个世纪前在按摩院度过那一夜后至今无法释怀的女人，

sentences.en: doesn't consider herself judgmental of others.
sentences.zh: 并不认为自己对他人的评判很苛刻。

sentences.en: But for decades, she's had trouble extending such compassion to herself.
sentences.zh: 但几十年来，她一直难以对自己给予同样的同情。

sentences.en: I was ashamed that I wasn't a strong enough person.
sentences.zh: 我为自己不够坚强而感到羞耻。

sentences.en: I said, no, I can't go.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，我不能去。

sentences.en: I got to do this.
sentences.zh: 我必须做这件事。

sentences.en: You know, I was ashamed of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我为此感到羞耻。

sentences.en: The hot-cold empathy gap makes other people feel more different from us than they actually are.
sentences.zh: “冷热共情差距”让别人感觉比实际上与我们更不同。

sentences.en: When someone does something we can't imagine that we would do,
sentences.zh: 当有人做了我们无法想象自己会做的事情时，

sentences.en: it's easy to be judgmental, to conclude they are weak, or worse, that they are bad people.
sentences.zh: 我们很容易去评判，断定他们软弱，或者更糟，断定他们是坏人。

sentences.en: This gap also makes us feel like strangers to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这种差距也让我们感觉自己像个陌生人。

sentences.en: So the next time we confidently
sentences.zh: 所以下次当我们自信满满地

sentences.en: announce that we would absolutely do this, or we would never do that, we would be wise to remember
sentences.zh: 宣称我们绝对会做这件事，或者绝不会做那件事时，我们最好记住

sentences.en: that the people we are now are very different
sentences.zh: 现在的我们与未来可能成为的我们

sentences.en: than the people we might become.
sentences.zh: 是非常不同的。
